related.name: Audio Dynamic Range & Data Rate Calculator

guidance: Component values only: the network is designed around one impedance per driver at one frequency, and a real driver's impedance moves with frequency, so measure it at the crossover before ordering parts. The slopes are electrical, the acoustic crossover is where the two drivers' own responses meet, and this page does not model sensitivity, cone breakup, directivity, off-axis summation, power handling, part tolerances or the values you can actually buy.
method: A passive two-way crossover puts a low-pass network in front of the woofer and a high-pass network in front of the tweeter, and a power amplifier's output impedance is low enough to treat as an ideal voltage source. A first-order (6 dB per octave) branch is one series reactance sized to equal the driver's impedance at the crossover frequency fc: L = Z / (2 pi fc) for the woofer's inductor and C = 1 / (2 pi fc Z) for the tweeter's capacitor, so each branch is 3 dB down at fc. A second-order (12 dB per octave) Butterworth branch adds a shunt element across the driver and scales both reactances by sqrt(2): the woofer gets L = sqrt(2) Z / (2 pi fc) in series and C = 1 / (sqrt(2) * 2 pi fc Z) across it, and the tweeter gets the mirrored pair, C = 1 / (sqrt(2) * 2 pi fc Z) in series and L = sqrt(2) Z / (2 pi fc) across it. Those values make each branch a maximally flat second-order section: 1 / sqrt(2) at fc, no peak anywhere, and 12 dB per octave beyond it, which the page's tests confirm by evaluating the exact two-element network against the analytic Butterworth magnitude. Tables that terminate the network with a source impedance equal to the driver's instead put twice the calculated capacitance in the low-pass shunt, which is why some published tables disagree on that one part while agreeing on the series elements. The tweeter pad is a constant-impedance L network: with the driver impedance Z and a voltage ratio k = 10^(-dB/20), the series resistor is Z (1 - k) and the shunt resistor is Z k / (1 - k), so the pad still presents Z to the high-pass branch and the network values above stand. Inputs are a crossover frequency from 100 to 10,000 Hz, a woofer and tweeter impedance from 1 to 32 ohms each and a tweeter level from 0 to 12 dB; decimal commas are accepted, and blank fields, text, a missing order and values outside those bounds are refused with the field named. Everything runs in the browser: no uploads, storage or network access.
